summary.intent: Monitor PR #352 for review comments and resolve them iteratively until no high-impact issues remain, then investigate and fix CI failures after merging to main.
summary.outcome: All 4 review threads resolved (3 code fixes + 1 low-impact CodeRabbit suggestion declined), codecov config added to mark desktop coverage as informational, and a Windows E2E test regex mismatch fixed on a new branch.

repo: Phase 23 extracted crypto, core, fuse, api-client, and sdk logic from apps/desktop/src-tauri into standalone Rust crates under crates/, leaving src-tauri as thin Tauri glue code
codecov.yml was absent before this session; the desktop flag was using auto threshold with 5% tolerance, which failed after Phase 23 extraction
The codecov/project/desktop check is non-blocking by convention in this repo (marked informational alongside api-client)
release-please scans all 329+ merge commits on main and can hit transient GitHub 5xx errors during backfill — rerunning resolves it
1Password SSH agent signing fails in agent subprocesses; retrying the commit directly works

code.finding: Test greps for 'Bin entry published for' but the actual log message emitted by cipherbox_fuse is 'Bin entry published' (no trailing 'for'), causing Windows E2E test 5 to fail
merge_folder_children is ~30 LOC map/merge logic already covered by 3 existing tests in apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/fuse/mod.rs; additional coverage not warranted

workflow: When resolving CodeRabbit comments requesting additional test coverage on trivial functions, replying with rationale and resolving without code changes is acceptable
After a large extraction refactor, codecov project-level checks need reconfiguration to reflect the new coverage distribution across components
gh run rerun can fix transient GitHub API 5xx failures in CI without any code changes

friction: 1Password SSH agent signing failure on first commit attempt required a manual retry

No codecov.yml existed in the repo, requiring creation from scratch to understand what thresholds were actually configured
Windows E2E log parsing was difficult — required multiple gh api calls to locate the specific failing test step and extract the grep pattern mismatch
